## Circular to Licensed Corporations which are licensed for Type 1 regulated activity

## Watch out!  Brokerage firms were defrauded again!

The Commission has issued a number of circulars to the brokerage firms and a press release  over  the  past  years  regarding  suspected  fraudulent  activities  targeted  at brokerage  firms.    In  the  previous  circulars  and  press  release,  the  Commission  has outlined the methods commonly used by fraudsters in defrauding brokerage firms and urged  brokerage  firms  to  adopt  proper  control  measures  to  guard  against  possible losses.

The  Commission  has  recently received certain reports from brokerage firms, informing us that some fraudsters again attempted to deceive brokerage firms.  Some brokerage firms did not suffer any losses because they had established the necessary control measures, but the others were less lucky.

This  circular  is  to  alert  brokerage  firms  again  regarding  the  suspected  fraudulent activities  and  the  possible  ways  to  strengthen  the  internal  control  environment  to avoid the potential losses arising from such activities.

## Common methods in deceiving brokerage firms

Fraudsters' methods in deceiving brokerage firms in the recently reported cases are no different from those mentioned in our previous circulars and press release:

- Fraudsters usually turned up in the guise of walk-in clients going to the offices of brokerage firms for opening stock trading accounts.  They would make use of  false/forged  identity  cards  and  proofs  of  address  for  covering  up  the  true identity and contact;
- Fraudsters  would  deposit  cheques  into  the  brokerage  firms'  bank  accounts directly and then produce deposit slips to the brokerage firms evidencing the deposit;
- Fraudsters would quickly place purchase instructions to the brokerage firms for  large  quantity  of  stocks  which  typically  would  be  speculative  or  thinly traded in the market before the cheques could be cleared;
- Cheques would then get bounced;

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

3 June 2004 Circular to Licensed Corporations which are licensed for Type 1 regulated activity Page 2

- Brokerage firms that had executed these purchase transactions without waiting for cleared funds could end up holding stocks which could not be disposed of in the market given thin trading, or could suffer from material trading loss due to a large drop in price; and
- Brokerage firms would not be able to locate these fraudsters given the false contact details provided.

When the above describes fraudulent activities recently reported by brokerage firms, brokerage  firms  should  also  be  mindful  of  possible  forged  cashiers'  orders  as fraudsters had also produced these to brokerage firms in the past.

## Useful hints for brokerage firms to avoid losses

The Commission reiterates the importance of the 'Know Your Clients' rules and of proper  control  procedures  in  handling  client's  orders,  particularly  in  the  course  of dealing  with  new  walk-in  clients.    Brokerage  firms  are  urged  to  adopt  appropriate control procedures to protect their interests.  The following are the basic procedures expected to be implemented:

- Carefully verify the identity document of client as well as his contact details. Do ask for sight of original address proof for your checking when in doubt;
- Make appropriate enquiries when a client places a large order for purchasing speculative stocks or stocks that are thinly traded; and
- Receive cleared funds before agreeing to execute large purchase orders for new walk-in clients.

Finally,  apart  from  reporting  suspected  fraudulent  activities  to  the  Commission, brokerage firms  are  also  reminded  to  report  such  cases  to  the  Police  for  its  further investigation.
